newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels block senior U.N. refugee official.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels block senior U.N. refugee official.

text.p: Zaire rebels blocked a senior U.N. official seeking access to Rwandan refugees, minutes after he said he hoped his talks with rebel authorities would bring greater access.

Rebels prevented Sergio Vieira de Mello, assistant high commissioner for the U.N. refugee agency (UNHCR), on Wednesday from travelling more than 42 km (25 miles) south of Kisangani where tens of thousands of Rwandan Hutus are believed stranded.
Officials of the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL) cited "security concerns".
De Mello, who arrived in Kisangani after talks in Lubumbashi with AFDL leaders, told Reuters he was optimistic aid agencies would soon be given better access to areas of Zaire containing refugees.
"We may have entered a new phase in our relationship," he said during a visit to Biaro refugee camp, south of Kisangani. "I'm hoping soon that the picture will become clearer."
But minutes later de Mello, accompanied by regional governor Yagi Sitolo and senior UNHCR officials, was blocked by rebel soldiers from travelling along a road leading farther south.
Sitolo did not speak to soldiers manning the roadblock, but later an AFDL official Emmanuel Kamanzi said they could not proceed because the area was unsafe.
"There has been a lot of fighting between soldiers and armed elements. We cannot guarantee your security if you proceed," Kamanzi said.
Aid officials said they were disappointed they had still not been able to pass the 42 km point, but said they hoped the message from Lubumbashi would filter through in coming days.
UNHCR voiced concern on Wednesday about reports of fresh killings of Rwandan refugees by the Tutsi-dominated rebels.
Aid workers have not been able to travel south of Biaro for weeks, following attacks on the refugee camps by Zairean villagers and rebel soldiers.
Refugees who fled the attacks on April 21 have spoken of hundreds, possibly thousands, of refugees being killed in the dense forests.
Since then refugees have been drifting back to Biaro to await a U.N. airlift back to Rwanda, which is likely to pass the 25,000 mark on Thursday.
Nearly 100,000 refugees gathered at Biaro and nearby Kasese camps before April 21, but following the attacks only around 40,000 have returned.
They are dying in their dozens at Biaro, with aid officials putting the death toll at nearly 50 a day since March.
De Mello said the UNHCR believed over 170,000 refugees are in Zaire in contrast to the Rwandan government which says just 30,000 remain.
A group of at least 6,000 was discovered at a village around 82 kms (50 miles) south of Kisangani at the weekend, many on the verge of death.

The refugees were among over 300,000 who fled west in October from camps on Zaire's border with Rwanda and Burundi rather than join more than a million other Hutu refugees from Zaire and Tanzania who returned home when Zairean rebels began their offensive.
They originally fled Rwanda in 1994 in fear of reprisals for the genocide of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus.
